investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All Available Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place the agent pod: 2 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. The pod remained unscheduled for ~147 seconds before the eval timed out, producing zero evidence and failing every required contract assertion.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry that resource class, and the other 4 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector rules. With 0/6 nodes available and preemption unable to free capacity, every new remote-agent pod is immediately Unschedulable. This prevented the eval runner from reaching the agent creation step, so no evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was ever written and all contract assertions failed. This is an eval-detected infrastructure capacity constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

failed-check.timing: latencyMs=154699, status=fail — the eval ran for ~154 s and ended at 2026-07-16T11:51:09.532Z without producing any evidence.
expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all four required fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are absent, confirming the runner never advanced past pod scheduling.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:254-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf [running, idle, ready]; neither assertion could be evaluated because the pod never started.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: all available VM slots are occupied by existing agents or workloads, leaving no capacity for new pods. Supported directly by the scheduler message in failed-check.message and both sibling check messages.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 remaining nodes do not satisfy the pod's affinity rules, meaning the schedulable pool is effectively limited to only the 2 kata-capable nodes. If those rules changed or node labels were removed, the effective capacity would shrink even if raw VM slots exist.

Tertiary — cluster under-provisioning: the total number of kata.peerpods.io/vm slots across the cluster is insufficient for the concurrent eval load plus any live workloads running at the time of the check (2026-07-16T11:48–11:56Z).

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All Available Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place the agent pod: 2 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. The pod remained unscheduled for ~147 seconds before the eval timed out, producing zero evidence and failing every required contract assertion.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry that resource class, and the other 4 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector rules. With 0/6 nodes available and preemption unable to free capacity, every new remote-agent pod is immediately Unschedulable. This prevented the eval runner from reaching the agent creation step, so no evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was ever written and all contract assertions failed. This is an eval-detected infrastructure capacity constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
proof: failed-check.message: '0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.' — the scheduler message is explicit about both failure modes.
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=154699, status=fail — the eval ran for ~154 s and ended at 2026-07-16T11:51:09.532Z without producing any evidence.
expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all four required fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are absent, confirming the runner never advanced past pod scheduling.
sibling.remote-agent-state: identical scheduler message, latencyMs=149594, status=fail — the state check hit the same scheduling wall.
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical scheduler message, latencyMs=149235, status=fail — the runtime check hit the same scheduling wall.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1880-1885: the runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) immediately after requireOrgId; if the pod never schedules, no downstream evidence can be written.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:254-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf [running, idle, ready]; neither assertion could be evaluated because the pod never started.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: all available VM slots are occupied by existing agents or workloads, leaving no capacity for new pods. Supported directly by the scheduler message in failed-check.message and both sibling check messages.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 remaining nodes do not satisfy the pod's affinity rules, meaning the schedulable pool is effectively limited to only the 2 kata-capable nodes. If those rules changed or node labels were removed, the effective capacity would shrink even if raw VM slots exist.

Tertiary — cluster under-provisioning: the total number of kata.peerpods.io/vm slots across the cluster is insufficient for the concurrent eval load plus any live workloads running at the time of the check (2026-07-16T11:48–11:56Z).

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: 0/6 nodes are available due to 2 nodes reporting Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm resources and 4 nodes not matching the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the agent pod could not be scheduled, the eval runner never reached the point of creating an agent or invoking the runtime, so zero evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) were returned and the expected-output contract was entirely unmet.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature in production-api has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource capacity on the two nodes that match the pod's node affinity/selector. The remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector constraints, and preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist on the eligible nodes. As a result, every remote agent pod submitted by the eval runner is stuck Unschedulable, preventing agent creation and all downstream checks from executing. This is a cluster-level infrastructure resource exhaustion localized to the remote-agents scheduling path, not a code defect in the eval runner or contract definitions. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence; this is an eval-layer failure reflecting a real infrastructure constraint.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 affinity-eligible nodes: the cluster has consumed all available peer-pod VM slots on the nodes that match the remote-agent pod's node affinity/selector, leaving no capacity for new pods. Preemption is not possible because no lower-priority pods occupy those nodes.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 remaining nodes do not match the pod's affinity/selector, which may indicate a node label was removed, a taint was added, or the pod spec's affinity rules were tightened, reducing the schedulable node pool from a larger set to only 2 nodes.

Tertiary — insufficient cluster scale-out: the cluster may not have auto-scaling configured or triggered for the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource type, so new nodes with available VM capacity were not provisioned before the scheduling timeout.

Lower confidence — eval runner token or org resolution issue: the runner does check for args.token before proceeding (run-status-probes.mjs:1915), but the scheduler error message is explicit and appears before any API call could be made, making a token issue an unlikely primary cause for this run.

If resource exhaustion is confirmed, free VM slots by terminating idle or stale remote-agent pods, or provision additional nodes with kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity to restore scheduling headroom.
Investigate whether cluster auto-scaling is configured for the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource type and, if not, evaluate enabling it to prevent recurrence.

Monitor the remote-agents feature status in the observability dashboard; with degradedAfterFailures=1 and all three checks failing, the feature will be flagged as degraded or in outage until scheduling recovers.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe nodes shows that kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity is available and not exhausted on the 2 affinity-eligible nodes, the scheduling failure has a different cause (e.g., a quota policy, admission webhook, or runtime class misconfiguration).

If the 4 nodes that 'didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector' are shown to have always been excluded by a stable, intentional affinity rule, then the root cause is purely resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes rather than any affinity drift.
If a subsequent eval run succeeds (all 5 evidence fields present and message contains 'hello from aura') without any cluster changes, the exhaustion was transient and self-resolved.

If the remote-agent-create sibling check passes while remote-agent-runtime fails, the failure is not a shared scheduling dependency and a different cause (e.g., runtime-specific configuration) should be investigated.

If the eval runner logs show the probe returned a SKIP status due to a missing token (run-status-probes.mjs:1915) rather than a scheduling error, the scheduling message would be an artifact of a different code path.
